DECISION: split into four children, three of them new lemmas and one a reused accepted declaration. The parent's frozen type follows from them by the supplied proof's Steps 6–7, and every one of them is used.

PARENT ASSEMBLY (what the parent proves from the children). Let r := max(R,0)+1.
1. Apply cutoff_radial (iwl_cr_ce_cutoff_radial_operator) with P, m, r. Its hypothesis (H) is discharged by the parent's own frozen dependency iwl_cr_radial_operator P m m, dropping item (ii). This gives a linear Φ : D^{m+1} → D^m that maps null sequences to null sequences and satisfies the Hω-formula on B_r(0).
2. Define C := X ∘ Φ (toCurrent := X.toCurrent.comp Φ). It is sequentially continuous by (a) and X.continuous'.
3. Cone property. Given ω, ψ and N open ⊇ spt X with the Hω-formula on N, put N′ := N ∩ B_r(0). It is open and contains spt X, since spt X ⊆ B̄_R(0) ⊆ B_r(0). On N′, ψ(x) = Φ(ω)(x) (ext over v). So locality (iwl_cr_ce_apply_eq_of_eqOn_nhds_support) gives X(ψ) = X(Φ(ω)) = C(ω).
The vanishing lemma is used only through locality.

WHY THESE CHILDREN. The supplied proof combines three independent, standard obligations, each reusable beyond this node:
(1) locality: a current only sees a test form near its support. This is Step 7, and also the "independent of ζ" remark after Simon 2.23. Every sibling cone node (cone_boundary, cone_estimates, cone_im) and the smooth push-forward branch quantifies over test forms that agree on an open N ⊇ spt.
(2) cutoff_null: the Leibniz estimate of Step 5 for a fixed C_c^∞ cut-off. Multiplication by ζ maps C^∞-null sequences on tsupport ζ to null sequences of test forms. Every current of the form ω ↦ X(ζ·Lω) needs it (Simon 2.23 push-forwards, cut-off extensions).
(3) cutoff_radial: Steps 1–5, the operator Φ(ω) = ζ·Hω. The cone siblings need such a concrete test form satisfying the Hω-formula near spt X.
(4) vanish_off_support: the comparator-accepted isoperimetric_apply_eq_zero_of_disjoint_support, reused with a byte-identical frozen type (no new node). It is needed by (1). Its record is copied from the accepted cycle_reduction decomposition-v2.

subproblems.title: Currents annihilate test forms supported off their support (reused accepted lemma)
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ, every set U ⊆ ℝ^P, every current T ∈ GeometricCurrentOn U n and every test form ω ∈ TestFormOn U n: if tsupport ω is disjoint from spt T = U ∖ zeroRegion(T), then T(ω) = 0. (Reuse, with identical frozen Lean type, of the comparator-accepted declaration isoperimetric_apply_eq_zero_of_disjoint_support.)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n), Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n)) T.support → T ω = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the accepted proof of the reused declaration isoperimetric_apply_eq_zero_of_disjoint_support (node root.isoperimetric-a1.vanish_off_support-a1), reproduced verbatim; the frozen Lean type is identical, so the comparator-accepted declaration is reused.

Notation. For T ∈ GeometricCurrentOn U n, `T.VanishesOn W` means T(η) = 0 for every η ∈ TestFormOn U n with tsupport η ⊆ W. Let 𝒲 be the family of all W ⊆ ℝ^P with W open, closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U and T.VanishesOn W. By definition T.zeroRegion = ⋃𝒲 and T.support = U ∖ T.zeroRegion.

1. Let K := tsupport ω. Since ω ∈ TestFormOn U n, ω is C^∞, has compact support (so K is compact, in particular closed) and K ⊆ U.
2. K ⊆ ⋃𝒲. Let x ∈ K. Then x ∈ U, and x ∉ T.support by the disjointness hypothesis, i.e. x ∉ U ∖ T.zeroRegion; hence x ∈ T.zeroRegion = ⋃𝒲.
3. Every member of 𝒲 is open, so by compactness of K there are finitely many W_1, …, W_r ∈ 𝒲 (r ≥ 0; r = 0 when K = ∅) with K ⊆ W_1 ∪ ⋯ ∪ W_r (e.g. `IsCompact.elim_finite_subcover_image`; it is convenient to index the cover by the resulting finite subfamily rather than by Fin r).
4. ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P), with the model with corners 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ^P), is a finite-dimensional, Hausdorff, σ-compact smooth manifold, and K is closed and covered by the open sets W_i (i ranging over the finite index set of step 3). Hence there is a smooth partition of unity on K subordinate to (W_i): C^∞ functions ψ_1, …, ψ_r : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with tsupport ψ_i ⊆ W_i for every i and Σ_i ψ_i(x) = 1 for every x ∈ K (Mathlib `SmoothPartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate`; a real-valued `ContMDiff 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ^P) 𝓘(ℝ)` function of class C^∞ is `ContDiff ℝ ∞` by `contMDiff_iff_contDiff`).
5. For each i put η_i(x) := ψ_i(x) • ω(x). Then η_i is C^∞ (a C^∞ scalar function times a C^∞ form). If ω(x) = 0 or ψ_i(x) = 0 then η_i(x) = 0, so support η_i ⊆ support ω ∩ support ψ_i; taking closures, tsupport η_i ⊆ K ∩ tsupport ψ_i ⊆ U ∩ W_i. In particular η_i has compact support (closed subset of the compact K). Thus η_i ∈ TestFormOn U n and tsupport η_i ⊆ W_i.
6. Since W_i ∈ 𝒲, T vanishes on W_i, so T(η_i) = 0 for every i.
7. ω = Σ_i η_i in TestFormOn U n (checked pointwise). If x ∈ K, then Σ_i ψ_i(x) • ω(x) = (Σ_i ψ_i(x)) • ω(x) = ω(x). If x ∉ K, then x ∉ support ω, so ω(x) = 0 and every η_i(x) = 0. (If r = 0 then K = ∅, ω = 0 and both sides are 0.)
8. T acts ℝ-linearly on TestFormOn U n (T.toCurrent is a linear map), so by steps 6 and 7, T(ω) = Σ_i T(η_i) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: tsupport ω is a compact subset of U disjoint from spt T, hence contained in the zero region, i.e. covered by the open sets W on which T vanishes.
Extract a finite subcover W_1, …, W_r of tsupport ω.
Take a smooth partition of unity ψ_1, …, ψ_r on tsupport ω subordinate to the W_i (Mathlib SmoothPartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate).
Each ψ_i • ω is a test form in U with tsupport in W_i, so T(ψ_i • ω) = 0.
ω = Σ_i ψ_i • ω pointwise, so T(ω) = 0 by linearity.

subproblems.title: Locality of currents: test forms that agree near the support have the same value
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set, T ∈ D_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n), ψ, φ ∈ D^n(U) (TestFormOn U n), and let N ⊆ ℝ^P be an open set with spt T ⊆ N. If ψ(x) = φ(x) for every x ∈ N, then T(ψ) = T(φ).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ψ φ : TestFormOn U n) (N : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen N → T.support ⊆ N → (∀ x ∈ N, (ψ : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) x = (φ : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) x) → T ψ = T φ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^P := Eucl P. D^n(U) := TestFormOn U n is the real submodule of C^∞ n-forms ω : ℝ^P → Λ_n with compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ U; addition, subtraction and scalar multiplication are pointwise. D_n(U) := GeometricCurrentOn U n; its underlying map T.toCurrent : D^n(U) → ℝ is ℝ-linear, and T(ω) means T.toCurrent ω. spt T := T.support. tsupport f := closure(support f), where support f = {x : f(x) ≠ 0}.

Source: Step 7 of the parent proof, where ψ − Φ(ω) vanishes on an open neighbourhood N′ of spt X. Here it is stated for arbitrary U, T, ψ, φ and N. This is the locality behind Simon's remark after 2.23 that f_#T(ω) = T(ζ f^#ω) does not depend on the cut-off ζ.

1. Put η := ψ − φ. It lies in D^n(U), because a submodule is closed under subtraction, and η(x) = ψ(x) − φ(x) for every x ∈ ℝ^P.
2. For x ∈ N the hypothesis gives η(x) = ψ(x) − φ(x) = 0. Hence support η ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ N.
3. ℝ^P ∖ N is closed because N is open. The closure of a set is contained in every closed superset, so tsupport η = closure(support η) ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ N (Lean: `closure_minimal` with `IsOpen.isClosed_compl`).
4. Since spt T ⊆ N, the set ℝ^P ∖ N is disjoint from spt T. By step 3, tsupport η is also disjoint from spt T (`Set.disjoint_of_subset_left`, `Set.disjoint_compl_left_iff_subset`).
5. Apply the sibling isoperimetric_apply_eq_zero_of_disjoint_support to P, n, U, T and the test form η. By step 4 its hypothesis holds, so T(η) = 0.
6. T.toCurrent is ℝ-linear, so T(η) = T(ψ − φ) = T(ψ) − T(φ) (`map_sub`). By step 5, T(ψ) − T(φ) = 0, i.e. T(ψ) = T(φ). ∎
proof_key_steps: η := ψ − φ is a test form in U that vanishes on the open set N.
Hence tsupport η ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ N, a closed set disjoint from spt T ⊆ N.

subproblems.title: Multiplying by a fixed cut-off turns C^∞-null sequences into null sequences of test forms
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ and U ⊆ ℝ^P. Let ζ : ℝ^P → ℝ be C^∞ with compact support and tsupport ζ ⊆ U. Let (ψ_l)_{l ∈ ℕ} be C^∞ k-forms ψ_l : ℝ^P → Λ_k, and (φ_l)_{l ∈ ℕ} test forms in D^k(U) (TestFormOn U k) with φ_l(x) = ζ(x)ψ_l(x) for all l and x. Suppose that for every j ∈ ℕ and every ε > 0 there is l₀ with ‖D^jψ_l(x)‖ ≤ ε for all l ≥ l₀ and all x ∈ tsupport ζ. Then TestFormOnConverges φ 0. That is, there is a compact K ⊆ U with tsupport φ_l ⊆ K for every l and tsupport 0 ⊆ K, such that D^jφ_l → D^j0 = 0 uniformly on K for every j ∈ ℕ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (ζ : Eucl P → ℝ) (ψs : ℕ → DifferentialForm (Eucl P) k) (φs : ℕ → TestFormOn U k), ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) ζ → HasCompactSupport ζ → tsupport ζ ⊆ U → (∀ l, ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) (ψs l)) → (∀ l x, (φs l : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) k) x = ζ x • ψs l x) → (∀ (j : ℕ) (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ l in atTop, ∀ x ∈ tsupport ζ, ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ j (ψs l) x‖ ≤ ε) → TestFormOnConverges φs 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^P := Eucl P. Λ_k := Covector (ℝ^P) k, with its operator norm. D^j := iteratedFDeriv ℝ j, with the operator norm ‖·‖ of continuous multilinear maps. C^∞ means ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞). D^k(U) := TestFormOn U k. TestFormOnConverges φ 0 means: there is a compact K ⊆ U such that tsupport φ_l ⊆ K for all l, tsupport 0 ⊆ K, and for every j, D^jφ_l → D^j0 uniformly on K as l → ∞.

Source: Step 5 of the parent proof (the Leibniz estimate for ζψ), isolated for an arbitrary cut-off ζ and sequence (ψ_l).

1. (The compact set.) Put K := tsupport ζ. It is compact because ζ has compact support, and K ⊆ U by hypothesis.
2. (Supports.) For each l, φ_l = (x ↦ ζ(x)•ψ_l(x)) as functions (funext of the hypothesis). If ζ(x) = 0 then φ_l(x) = 0, so support φ_l ⊆ support ζ. Taking closures, tsupport φ_l ⊆ tsupport ζ = K (`tsupport_smul_subset_left`). The zero test form is the zero function, whose tsupport is ∅ ⊆ K (`tsupport_zero`).
3. (The limit.) The iterated derivatives of the zero function vanish: D^j0 = 0 for every j (`iteratedFDeriv_fun_zero`). So for each fixed j ∈ ℕ it remains to show: for every ε > 0 there is l₀ with ‖D^jφ_l(x)‖ < ε for all l ≥ l₀ and all x ∈ K. This is uniform convergence to 0 on K (`Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff`, using dist(0, y) = ‖y‖). Fix j and ε > 0.
4. (Bounds for ζ.) Let i ∈ ℕ. D^iζ is continuous because ζ is C^∞ (`ContDiff.continuous_iteratedFDeriv`). It has compact support, since support D^iζ ⊆ tsupport ζ (`HasCompactSupport.iteratedFDeriv`). A continuous function with compact support is bounded, so there is Z_i ∈ ℝ with ‖D^iζ(x)‖ ≤ Z_i for all x (`Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support`). Moreover Z_i ≥ ‖D^iζ(0)‖ ≥ 0.
5. Put A := Σ_{i=0}^{j} C(j,i)·Z_i ≥ 0 and δ := ε/(2(A+1)) > 0.
6. (Smallness of ψ_l.) Let i ∈ {0, …, j}. The hypothesis with order j − i and tolerance δ gives l_i such that ‖D^{j−i}ψ_l(x)‖ ≤ δ for all l ≥ l_i and x ∈ K. There are finitely many i, so l₀ := max_i l_i works for all of them (`Filter.eventually_all_finset`): for l ≥ l₀, every i ≤ j and every x ∈ K, ‖D^{j−i}ψ_l(x)‖ ≤ δ.
7. (Leibniz bound.) ζ and ψ_l are C^∞ and j ≤ ∞, so for every x:
   ‖D^j(y ↦ ζ(y)•ψ_l(y))(x)‖ ≤ Σ_{i=0}^{j} C(j,i)·‖D^iζ(x)‖·‖D^{j−i}ψ_l(x)‖.
   In Lean this is `norm_iteratedFDeriv_smul_le` from Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.ContDiff.Bounds; add `import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.ContDiff.Bounds` to Submission.lean.
8. (The estimate.) Let l ≥ l₀ and x ∈ K. All factors in step 7 are nonnegative, so steps 2, 4, 6 and 7 give
   ‖D^jφ_l(x)‖ ≤ Σ_{i=0}^{j} C(j,i)·Z_i·δ = Aδ = Aε/(2(A+1)) < ε.
   The last inequality holds because Aε < 2(A+1)ε, as A ≥ 0 and ε > 0.
9. Steps 1–3 and 8 are exactly TestFormOnConverges φ 0, with the compact set K ⊆ U. ∎
proof_key_steps: K := tsupport ζ is compact and ⊆ U, and it contains tsupport φ_l = tsupport(ζψ_l) for every l, as well as tsupport 0 = ∅.
Each D^iζ is continuous with compact support, hence bounded by some Z_i.
For fixed j and ε, choose l₀ so that ‖D^{j−i}ψ_l‖ ≤ δ := ε/(2(A+1)) on K for all i ≤ j and l ≥ l₀.
Leibniz bound on K: ‖D^j(ζψ_l)‖ ≤ Σ C(j,i)‖D^iζ‖‖D^{j−i}ψ_l‖ ≤ Aδ < ε.
Hence D^jφ_l → 0 = D^j0 uniformly on K for every j, i.e. TestFormOnConverges φ 0.

subproblems.title: The cut-off radial operator Φ(ω) = ζ·Hω on test forms
subproblems.statement:
Let P, m ∈ ℕ and r ∈ ℝ. Assume (H): for every C^∞ (m+1)-form ω : ℝ^P → Λ_{m+1} there is a C^∞ m-form ψ : ℝ^P → Λ_m such that
(i) ψ(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 t^m ω(tx)(x, v) dt for all x ∈ ℝ^P and v ∈ (ℝ^P)^m;
(iii) for all j ∈ ℕ and R, D ∈ ℝ with D ≥ 0: if ‖D^iω(y)‖ ≤ D for every i ≤ j and every y with ‖y‖ ≤ R, then ‖D^jψ(x)‖ ≤ (R + j)·D for every x with ‖x‖ ≤ R.
Then there is an ℝ-linear map Φ : D^{m+1}(ℝ^P) → D^m(ℝ^P) (test forms on univ) such that:
(a) for every sequence (ω_l) of (m+1)-test forms, TestFormOnConverges ω 0 implies TestFormOnConverges (l ↦ Φ(ω_l)) 0;
(b) Φ(ω)(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 t^m ω(tx)(x, v) dt for every ω ∈ D^{m+1}(ℝ^P), every x in the open ball B_r(0) and every v ∈ (ℝ^P)^m.
Here (x, v) := Fin.cons x v. Hypothesis (H) is exactly the statement of iwl_cr_radial_operator instantiated at k := m, a := m, with its fderiv item (ii) removed. iwl_cr_radial_operator is the parent's own frozen dependency, not a child of this decomposition, and the parent discharges (H) with it.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (r : ℝ), (∀ ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) (m + 1), ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) ω → ∃ ψ : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) m, ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) ψ ∧ (∀ (x : Eucl P) (v : Fin m → Eucl P), ψ x v = ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, t ^ m * ω (t • x) (Fin.cons x v)) ∧ ∀ (j : ℕ) (R D : ℝ), 0 ≤ D → (∀ i ≤ j, ∀ y ∈ closedBall (0 : Eucl P) R, ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ i ω y‖ ≤ D) → ∀ x ∈ closedBall (0 : Eucl P) R, ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ j ψ x‖ ≤ (R + j) * D) → ∃ Φ : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) (m + 1) →ₗ[ℝ] TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) m, (∀ ωs : ℕ → TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) (m + 1), TestFormOnConverges ωs 0 → TestFormOnConverges (fun l => Φ (ωs l)) 0) ∧ ∀ (ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) (m + 1)) (x : Eucl P), x ∈ ball (0 : Eucl P) r → ∀ v : Fin m → Eucl P, (Φ ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) m) x v = ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, t ^ m * (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) (m + 1)) (t • x) (Fin.cons x v)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^P := Eucl P. Λ_k := Covector (ℝ^P) k. D^i := iteratedFDeriv ℝ i, with operator norms. C^∞ means ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞). D^k(ℝ^P) := TestFormOn univ k: C^∞ k-forms with compact support, a real submodule with pointwise operations. B_s(0) and B̄_s(0) are the open and closed balls. (x, v) := Fin.cons x v. TestFormOnConverges ω 0 means: there is a compact K ⊆ univ with tsupport ω_l ⊆ K for all l (and tsupport 0 ⊆ K), such that D^iω_l → D^i0 uniformly on K for every i.

Source: Steps 1–5 of the parent proof, together with the ζ = 1 part of Step 7. The parent's radius R₀ + 1 is replaced by an arbitrary r; the parent applies this lemma with r := max(R, 0) + 1.

1. (Radial forms.) Every ω ∈ D^{m+1}(ℝ^P) is C^∞. So (H) gives a C^∞ m-form ψ_ω satisfying (i) and (iii) for ω. Fix such a choice ω ↦ ψ_ω (axiom of choice; Lean `choose`).
2. (Integrability.) Let ω ∈ D^{m+1}(ℝ^P), x ∈ ℝ^P and w ∈ (ℝ^P)^{m+1}. The function t ↦ t^m·ω(tx)(w) is continuous on ℝ: t ↦ tx is continuous, ω is continuous, and evaluating a continuous alternating map at the fixed tuple w is continuous (`continuous_eval_const`). Hence it is interval integrable on [0, 1] (`Continuous.intervalIntegrable`).
3. (Linearity of ω ↦ ψ_ω.) Let ω, ω′ ∈ D^{m+1}(ℝ^P), c ∈ ℝ, x ∈ ℝ^P and v ∈ (ℝ^P)^m. The operations are pointwise. By (i), step 2 and additivity of the interval integral (`intervalIntegral.integral_add`):
   ψ_{ω+ω′}(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 t^m·(ω(tx)(x,v) + ω′(tx)(x,v)) dt = ψ_ω(x)(v) + ψ_{ω′}(x)(v).
   Pulling the constant out of the integral (`intervalIntegral.integral_const_mul`; no integrability needed):
   ψ_{cω}(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 t^m·(c·ω(tx)(x,v)) dt = c·ψ_ω(x)(v).
   A continuous alternating map is determined by its values (ext), and two forms that agree at every x are equal (funext). So ψ_{ω+ω′} = ψ_ω + ψ_{ω′} and ψ_{cω} = c·ψ_ω.
4. (Cut-off.) Put r₀ := max(r, 0) ≥ 0, so 0 < r₀ + 1 < r₀ + 2. ℝ^P is an inner product space, so `HasContDiffBump` holds and there is a ContDiffBump ζ centred at 0 with rIn = r₀ + 1 and rOut = r₀ + 2. It has the following properties:
   - ζ : ℝ^P → ℝ is C^∞ (`ContDiffBump.contDiff`);
   - ζ has compact support (`ContDiffBump.hasCompactSupport`, since ℝ^P is finite-dimensional);
   - tsupport ζ = B̄_{r₀+2}(0) (`ContDiffBump.tsupport_eq`);
   - ζ(x) = 1 whenever ‖x‖ ≤ r₀ + 1 (`ContDiffBump.one_of_mem_closedBall`).
5. (The operator.) For ω ∈ D^{m+1}(ℝ^P) put Φ(ω) := (x ↦ ζ(x)•ψ_ω(x)).
   - Φ(ω) is C^∞ (`ContDiff.smul` of the C^∞ functions ζ and ψ_ω).
   - tsupport Φ(ω) ⊆ tsupport ζ (`tsupport_smul_subset_left`). A closed subset of a compact set is compact (`IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset`), so Φ(ω) has compact support. Also tsupport Φ(ω) ⊆ univ.
   Thus Φ(ω) ∈ D^m(ℝ^P). By step 3, Φ(ω + ω′)(x) = ζ(x)•(ψ_ω(x) + ψ_{ω′}(x)) = Φ(ω)(x) + Φ(ω′)(x), and Φ(cω)(x) = ζ(x)•(c·ψ_ω(x)) = c·(ζ(x)•ψ_ω(x)) = c·Φ(ω)(x). Equality in the submodule is equality of the underlying forms (`Subtype.ext`), so Φ is an ℝ-linear map D^{m+1}(ℝ^P) → D^m(ℝ^P).
6. (Property (b).) Let ω ∈ D^{m+1}(ℝ^P), x ∈ B_r(0) and v ∈ (ℝ^P)^m. Then ‖x‖ < r ≤ r₀ < r₀ + 1, so ζ(x) = 1 by step 4. Hence Φ(ω)(x)(v) = (1•ψ_ω(x))(v) = ψ_ω(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 t^m ω(tx)(x, v) dt by (i).
7. (Property (a): setup.) Let (ω_l) be a sequence in D^{m+1}(ℝ^P) with TestFormOnConverges ω 0. Then there is a compact K with tsupport ω_l ⊆ K for every l, and for every i, D^iω_l → D^i0 = 0 uniformly on K (`iteratedFDeriv_fun_zero`).
   Apply the sibling iwl_cr_ce_cutoff_converges_zero with P, k := m, U := ℝ^P (univ), the cut-off ζ of step 4, ψ_l := ψ_{ω_l} and φ_l := Φ(ω_l). Its hypotheses hold as follows:
   - ζ is C^∞ with compact support and tsupport ζ ⊆ univ (step 4);
   - each ψ_{ω_l} is C^∞ (step 1);
   - φ_l(x) = ζ(x)•ψ_{ω_l}(x) for all l and x, by the definition of Φ (step 5).
   It remains to verify: for every j ∈ ℕ and ε > 0, eventually in l, ‖D^jψ_{ω_l}(x)‖ ≤ ε for all x ∈ tsupport ζ = B̄_{r₀+2}(0).
8. Fix j ∈ ℕ and ε > 0. Put D := ε/(r₀ + 2 + j); D > 0 because r₀ + 2 + j > 0.
9. (Global smallness of ω_l.) Fix i ≤ j. By uniform convergence on K there is l_i such that ‖D^iω_l(y)‖ < D for all l ≥ l_i and y ∈ K. If y ∉ K, then y ∉ tsupport ω_l; since support D^iω_l ⊆ tsupport ω_l (`support_iteratedFDeriv_subset`), D^iω_l(y) = 0 and ‖D^iω_l(y)‖ = 0 ≤ D. So ‖D^iω_l(y)‖ ≤ D for all l ≥ l_i and all y ∈ ℝ^P. There are finitely many i ≤ j, so put l₀ := max_{i ≤ j} l_i (`Filter.eventually_all_finset`).
10. (Radial bound.) Let l ≥ l₀. Then ‖D^iω_l(y)‖ ≤ D for every i ≤ j and every y, in particular for every y with ‖y‖ ≤ r₀ + 2. Apply (iii) to ω_l and ψ_{ω_l} with this j, R := r₀ + 2 and D ≥ 0: ‖D^jψ_{ω_l}(x)‖ ≤ (r₀ + 2 + j)·D = ε for every x with ‖x‖ ≤ r₀ + 2, i.e. for every x ∈ tsupport ζ.
11. Steps 7–10 verify every hypothesis of iwl_cr_ce_cutoff_converges_zero, which yields TestFormOnConverges (l ↦ Φ(ω_l)) 0. This is property (a).
12. Steps 5, 6 and 11 show that Φ has all the required properties. ∎
proof_key_steps: Choose ψ_ω for each test form ω by (H). By (i) and linearity of the interval integral (the integrands are continuous), ω ↦ ψ_ω is linear.
Fix a ContDiffBump ζ with ζ = 1 on B̄_{r₀+1}(0) and tsupport ζ = B̄_{r₀+2}(0), where r₀ = max(r, 0). Then Φ(ω) := ζψ_ω is a linear map D^{m+1} → D^m.
On B_r(0) ⊆ B̄_{r₀+1}(0) we have ζ = 1, so Φ(ω) satisfies the Hω-formula by (i).
If ω_l → 0, then for each j and ε, eventually ‖D^iω_l‖ ≤ ε/(r₀+2+j) everywhere for all i ≤ j. So by (iii), ‖D^jψ_{ω_l}‖ ≤ ε on tsupport ζ.
iwl_cr_ce_cutoff_converges_zero then gives Φ(ω_l) → 0 in D^m.
